dek: Jay-Z headlines the Super Bowl LXI halftime show on Feb. 14. Tarima ranked the 21 verses that built the legend, from No. 21 to No. 1.

slides.label: Where it started
slides.text: Every New York kid has a first Jay-Z album. For Den founder *Danny Silverio*, it was *Vol. 2... Hard Knock Life*, the one with "Reservoir Dogs." A Roc diamond poster on the wall. "That cocky flow gave me *confidence*. The triple entendres made me *think*."

slides.label: No. 21 to 19
slides.text: *21. Song Cry*: Too proud to cry, so he lets the record do it. *20. Murder to Excellence*: The higher he climbs, the fewer faces like his. *19. The Devil Is a Lie*: Flips the Illuminati talk back on whoever spreads it.

slides.label: No. 18 to 16
slides.text: *18. Legacy*: Blue Ivy asks what a will is. He answers with one. *17. Brooklyn's Finest*: Two Brooklyn legends trading lines. The rookie keeps up. *16. Moment of Clarity*: Skill vs. sales, and why he picked five million.

slides.label: No. 15 to 13
slides.text: *15. Kill Jay Z*: Puts his own ego on trial, in the second person. *14. December 4th*: His life story, narrated by his mother, Gloria Carter. *13. Drug Dealers Anonymous*: Answers a TV attack by owning his past out loud.

slides.label: No. 12 to 10
slides.text: *12. Renegade*: Tells critics who only hear the jewelry they're skimming. *11. 99 Problems*: Verse two is a whole traffic stop, in real time. *10. The Story of O.J.*: The $2M DUMBO building he passed on, now worth $25M.

slides.label: No. 9 to 7
slides.text: *9. Public Service Announcement*: The most famous reintroduction in rap. *8. Diamonds from Sierra Leone (Remix)*: The "business, man" verse boardrooms still quote. *7. Can I Live*: Go out enormous or don't go. His whole philosophy.

slides.label: No. 6 to 4
slides.text: *6. Dead Presidents II*: Why he chased the money, and what it already cost. *5. Takeover*: Does the math on Nas's catalog. The math hurts. *4. What's Free*: Freedom isn't a feeling. It's ownership.

slides.label: The top 3
slides.text: *3. Free Mason*: Shuts down the rumors, then marvels he made it out. *2. Seen It All*: Nobody can lecture him on the game. He lived it. *1. God Did*: Counts the billionaires out of his camp: him, Ye, Rihanna.

question: No. 1 bar: GOD DID or TAKEOVER? Pick one.

Before Hov takes the Super Bowl LXI stage on Feb. 14, Tarima ranked his 21 greatest bars, from No. 21 to No. 1.

Every New York kid has a first Jay-Z album. For Den founder Danny Silverio, it was Vol. 2... Hard Knock Life, the one with "Reservoir Dogs." That 1998 album was Jay's first to debut at No. 1, and it won the Grammy for Best Rap Album. Then came Rocawear on every block, a Roc diamond poster on the bedroom wall, the Kanye-produced beats on The Blueprint and that Panjabi MC remix. In Danny's words: "That cocky flow gave me confidence. The triple entendres made me think."

The list runs from solo classics to the guest verses where he walked onto somebody else's record and walked off with it: Takeover, Dead Presidents II, Can I Live, What's Free, and a top three of Free Mason, Seen It All and God Did.

No. 1 bar: GOD DID or TAKEOVER? Pick one.

Send this to the friend who still argues Reasonable Doubt over The Blueprint.

caption_linkedin:
Jay-Z will headline the Super Bowl LXI halftime show on Feb. 14, 2027. His company, Roc Nation, has produced the show since 2019. This is the first time he steps into the spotlight himself.

His catalog doubles as a business curriculum. On Meek Mill's "What's Free" (2018), he lists what he owns outright and defines freedom as ownership. On "The Story of O.J." (2017), he admits passing on a DUMBO building he could have bought for about $2 million, now worth around $25 million. Off the mic, he sold the Rocawear rights in 2007 for $204 million and bought them back in 2019 for $15 million.

Our Tarima desk ranked his 21 greatest bars. The lesson running through the list: equity outlasts income.
